Description: A marble inscription removed from the Vardar Gate at Thessalonica, listing six politarchs — the city's magistrates — in the first century AD. The title appears in no classical author, and critics once called Luke's use of it in Acts 17 an error. At least twenty-eight further stones from Macedonia repeat the title, several dated to the Julio-Claudian era, and Thessalonian coins carry it too.
BiblicalSignificance: When the mob dragged Jason before the 'city officials' in Acts 17, Luke used a word nobody else in ancient literature used — and he used it correctly, for exactly that city, in exactly that period. It is a small title, but it is the kind of detail only someone who had been there would get right.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the inscriptions confirm ‘politarch’ as a real Macedonian civic title in the first century, vindicating Luke’s term in Acts 17.
